opportunities.name: GitHub developer lead research and email draft
opportunities.description: Search GitHub for a given username, open their profile to note follower count and top repo stats, then compose a lead email to hiring@example.com with subject 'Lead for <role>: <username>' and a stats summary body.
steps: Open github.com and click the Search box
Type the <username> and submit the search
Click the 'Users' filter in the left sidebar
Click the matching user in the results to open their profile
Read follower count, top/pinned repo (stars, language) and latest post/activity
Open the New message compose page
Enter body '<username>: <followers> followers, top repo <repo> (<stars> stars, <language>), latest post: <post title>.'

instances.values: username=karpathy, role=ML Research Engineer, body: 226k followers, nanoGPT (63.8k stars, Python), latest post microgpt (interrupted by weather.com browsing 252–275s)
username=gaearon, role=Staff Frontend Engineer, body: 94k followers, react/react (251.1k stars, JavaScript), latest post 'How I Vibed a Proof of Conway's Conjecture'
username=simonw, role=Developer Advocate, body: 17.3k followers, llm (12.6k stars, Python), latest post 'Hello Python 3.15, goodbye 3.10...'

opportunities.name: Wikipedia person + Wayback Machine homepage note
opportunities.description: Look up a person on Wikipedia for a short bio, look up their related organisation's website homepage in a given year via the Wayback Machine to get the headline, then add a combined line to the Notes app.
steps: On Wikipedia, click the search box and type <person name>
Select the person from the suggestions and read birth date / role
Go to web.archive.org and enter <domain> in the Wayback URL box
Click a capture date in the calendar (early in the year)
Read the main headline on the archived homepage
Open the Notes app and click 'New note'
Type '<person>: born <date>, <role>. <domain> in <year>: <headline>' and press Enter
